parameters.jsCode:
const meta = $('Normalize Input').first().json;
const sourceText = items
  .map(i => i.json)
  .sort((a, b) => (a.index ?? 0) - (b.index ?? 0))
  .map(i => i.text)
  .filter(Boolean)
  .join('\n\n');
return [{ json: {
  title: meta.title,
  spaceKey: meta.spaceKey,
  template: meta.template,
  mode: meta.mode,
  pageUrl: meta.pageUrl,
  instructions: meta.instructions,
  confluenceBaseUrl: meta.confluenceBaseUrl,
  notify: meta.notify,
  mattermostChannelId: meta.mattermostChannelId,
  senderEmail: meta.senderEmail,
  parentPageId: meta.parentPageId,
  sourceText
} }];

options.systemMessage:
You write clean XHTML-compatible standard HTML for a Confluence page body. Use only standard tags such as h1, h2, h3, p, ul, ol, li, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td, code, pre, strong, em, a, br, hr. Close every non-void tag. Write void tags as self-closing XHTML tags:
and
. Preserve http, https, mailto, and relative href values on a tags. Escape < and > inside code and pre content. Write punctuation and symbols as Unicode characters (en dash, arrows, quotes), not HTML named entities such as   – → “. Do NOT use Confluence-specific XML, ac:structured-macro, ac:macro, ac:parameter, or any ac: namespace tags. Do not use script, iframe, event-handler attributes, or markdown formatting. Do not wrap the output in markdown code fences. Output only the HTML body content.

parameters.content:
### Template prompts
Edit the **Templates** node to list and customize how each `template` value writes the page.

Keys: `release-notes`, `wiki`, `doc`, `general`.
Unknown keys fall back to `general`. Publish after editing so production uses the new prompts.

options.systemMessage: You write structured JSON content for a MarTech announcement template. Output ONLY valid JSON matching the exact schema requested — no markdown code fences, no explanatory prose before or after. Adapt which sections you populate based on the announcement type guidance provided in the prompt — do not force irrelevant sections to have content just to fill them. whats_new and steps descriptions should be one to two sentences each. improvements and fixes are short one-line strings. Set action_required to null if there's nothing the reader needs to do. Set version, status_label, date, and related_link to null if not applicable — do not invent values. If a product name is provided, reference it naturally in the title or TL;DR; if not, write as a general MarTech team announcement without inventing a product.
